name: Citizenship via Simplified Declaration (Multiple Citizenship, Article 5-1)

qualifying_event.description: Since a new Article 5-1 of the Law on Citizenship took effect on 16 January 2026, Ukraine officially recognises multiple citizenship in specific cases: citizens of Poland, the Czech Republic, Germany, Canada, and the USA may acquire Ukrainian citizenship through a simplified declaration procedure rather than full naturalisation, and family members of foreign military personnel serving Ukraine or of deceased Ukrainian soldiers may submit a declaration renouncing foreign citizenship instead of proving its termination.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Proof of qualifying nationality (Poland/Czech Republic/Germany/Canada/USA) or documentation of the military-connected family relationship.

requirement_groups.name: Citizen of a designated country (Poland, Czech Republic, Germany, Canada, USA)

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant holds citizenship of Poland, the Czech Republic, Germany, Canada, or the USA.

requirement_groups.name: Family of foreign military personnel serving Ukraine or of deceased Ukrainian soldiers

requirements.blocker_text: Family member of foreign military personnel serving Ukraine, or of a Ukrainian soldier who died in service.

Files a declaration renouncing foreign citizenship, rather than having to prove its actual termination -- current holders who acquired Ukrainian citizenship since 1 January 2018 have until 16 July 2026 to file this declaration.

evidence_required.document: Proof of designated nationality (for the country-based track)
Documentation of the military-connected family relationship (for the family track)

sources.title: State Migration Service of Ukraine -- new multiple-citizenship rules effective 16 January 2026 (Article 5-1): simplified declaration procedure for citizens of Poland, Czech Republic, Germany, Canada, and USA; renunciation-declaration relief for military-connected family members; 16 July 2026 deadline for existing citizens (naturalised since 1 January 2018) to file declarations; expanded loss-of-citizenship grounds for national-security threats and armed aggression against Ukraine

STATUS: DRAFT -- this is an extremely recent legal change (effective just under 8 months before this build) sourced to a single tier-1 page; no second source was found to corroborate the exact designated-country list or the procedural mechanics of the declaration itself, and a separate tier-1 fetch (kmu.gov.ua's implementation-algorithm article) covered different accelerated-citizenship categories (merit, contract military service, foreign instructors, wartime aid) without mentioning this country-list provision at all -- not a contradiction, but thin enough independent corroboration that draft status is warranted for a change this significant. Categorized as 'family' since the military-family track is the more war-relevant, human-stakes case, though the designated-nationality track has nothing to do with family ties -- these are modeled as two OR-branch requirement groups in one file since they share the same amending source and the same dual-citizenship outcome. The 16 July 2026 declaration deadline for existing naturalised citizens is itself worth flagging: someone who naturalised between 1 Jan 2018 and 16 Jan 2026 and wants to keep dual status needs to act before that date, a time-sensitive detail not modeled as a blocking requirement here (it applies to already-naturalised citizens revisiting their status, not to new applicants) but worth surfacing.
